 Follow Us On: News Movies Bollywood Ramayana's Rs 2,000 crore budget and Rs 5,000 crore break-even gamble Rs 2,000-crore Ramayana needs Rs 5,000 crore to break even: Box office maths decoded
 With a reported Rs 2,000-crore budget, Ramayana Part I faces a box-office mountain few Indian films have dared to climb. From the Rs 100-crore opening-day target and advance-booking expectations to the staggering Rs 5,000-crore break-even estimate, here's the business maths behind Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious epic.
 Advertisement A poster of Ramayana featuring Yash as Raavana, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Ravie Dubey as Laxman By: Vineeta Kumar New Delhi , Oct 23, 2026 11:21 IST Last Updated Oct 23, 2026 11:21 IST Published by Vineeta Kumar Oct 23, 2026 08:17 IST A film can open to packed theatres, dominate social media and still have a mountain to climb before it becomes a financial success. For Ramayana Part I: Rise of Legend , that mountain is reportedly worth Rs 2,000 crore.
 The film's advance bookings opened almost 14 days ahead of its big Diwali release, giving audiences an early chance to build the kind of momentum the makers need to justify its mammoth budget. But how does a film pull off a task of this scale? Is a massive box-office opening enough? And how much does Ramayana Part I really need to rake in through advance bookings to set itself up for a strong opening at the ticket window?
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story India Today Digital spoke to trade expert Ramesh Bala to decode the box-office maths of Ramayana and understand how far the film is from setting itself on the path to financial success. Ramayana's advance booking: Is it on the right track?
 As of 2:20 pm on Thursday, October 22, Ramayana had sold around 1.33 lakh tickets, grossing Rs 7.52 crore across 3,749 shows in India, reported Sacnilk . However, advance bookings have not yet opened across many screens, making this preliminary data rather than a definitive indicator of the film's box-office prospects.
 The early numbers suggest that the film could be on the right track, provided it sustains its momentum and, more importantly, builds on it over the coming week. That period will be crucial in determining how strongly Ramayana opens at the box office.
 When asked for a ballpark figure, Bala suggested that the film would need to generate domestic advance bookings in the range of Rs 75–100 crore for its opening day.
 He explained why: "With its reported Rs 2,000 crore budget, Ramayana needs a massive opening. India advance bookings of Rs 75–100 crore and worldwide pre-sales of Rs 150–200 crore would create tremendous momentum." Word-of-mouth will be crucial for Ramayana
 This is where word of mouth becomes even more crucial for Ramayana than for several other big-ticket films that have made their mark in Indian cinema, including Pushpa, KGF and Baahubali . With a reported budget that makes it the most expensive Indian film to date, the stakes are exceptionally high. Its word of mouth will need to be equally powerful if the film is to sustain its box-office run beyond the opening weekend.
 "The film's star power, universal appeal and global reach could drive a historic opening, but strong word of mouth will be crucial for long-term success," Bala noted.
 While advance bookings appear to be picking up, much of the early business is currently coming from the Hindi market. For Ramayana to maximise its domestic box-office potential, it will also need strong support from the South Indian markets. A pan-India film of this scale cannot afford to rely on just one market to drive its opening-day numbers. So, what would that contribution need to look like?
 advertisement According to Bala, the South Indian markets would need to account for around 35-40 per cent of Ramayana 's total domestic advance bookings. In other words, if the film is targeting Rs 100 crore in domestic pre-sales, around Rs 35-40 crore would need to come from the South Indian markets alone.
 That is a mammoth task. Allu Arjun's Pushpa 2 remains the benchmark for domestic advance bookings, with gross pre-sales of Rs 91.24 crore, of which Rs 53.94 crore came from the South Indian markets.
 While Ramayana has the potential to challenge these numbers, matching or surpassing them through advance bookings alone will be no easy feat.
 Bala explained, "South India could contribute around 35-40 per cent of Ramayana 's total domestic advance bookings, with Karnataka and the Telugu states playing a major role, thanks to Yash's popularity and the film's universal appeal."
 How big does Ramayana need to open?
 When it comes to opening-day expectations, the sky appears to be the limit for Ramayana: Rise of Legend . Even if the film manages to generate Rs 75-100 crore in domestic advance bookings, it would still need a strong turnout from walk-in audiences to translate that pre-release momentum into a formidable opening-day total.
 advertisement Bala believes that an opening of at least Rs 100–125 crore nett (gross minus taxes) in India would be an ideal start, with the worldwide box office adding another crucial dimension to the film's performance.
 "Considering its massive budget, an opening day of Rs 100–125 crore nett in India and Rs 175–200 crore gross worldwide would be an ideal start. The film needs a historic opening followed by strong word of mouth to justify its unprecedented scale," Bala said.
 The overseas market will be another major piece of the puzzle. Ramayana will need to establish a strong international presence from the outset, with its worldwide previews on November 4 offering an early indication of how it is being received beyond India. A strong overseas opening could significantly bolster its global box-office prospects. Can Ramayana recover its Rs 2,000-crore budget?
 That brings us to the biggest question of all: how much does Ramayana Part I need to earn over its lifetime run to emerge as a profitable venture?
 The answer, at least on paper, is a staggering number. And it brings us to the question of the film's break-even point.
 advertisement In trade terms, a film's break-even point is the stage at which its revenues are sufficient to cover its costs, leaving it neither in profit nor in loss. These costs can include production and marketing expenses, although the exact calculation varies depending on the film's financing and distribution arrangements.
 For Ramayana , a simple calculation based on the reported Rs 2,000-crore budget and the commonly cited 2.5-times multiplier would put the worldwide box-office target at around Rs 5,000 crore. However, this is an indicative estimate rather than a confirmed break-even figure, as the actual calculation depends on the film's cost structure, revenue-sharing arrangements and non-theatrical earnings.
 Bala explained, "Going by the reported Rs 2,000 crore budget and the 2.5x calculation, Ramayana Part I would need approximately Rs 5,000 crore worldwide. That's an extraordinary target, even by global standards. While the film has massive potential with its star cast, universal appeal and international reach, achieving such numbers would be extremely challenging."
 However, a film's profitability does not depend solely on its box-office performance. Other revenue streams can help the makers recover their investment and potentially turn the project into a profitable venture.
 advertisement Bala added, "Theatrical collections alone won't determine profitability, as satellite, digital and other rights will also play a crucial role."
 The big gamble that is Ramayana
 This is, of course, only an early assessment. What Ramayana ultimately achieves at the box office, and how audiences receive it, remains difficult to predict at this stage.
 The buzz is high, the expectations are even higher, and the ambition is sky-high. If Ramayana manages to maximise its business across domestic and overseas markets, it could set a box-office benchmark that Indian cinema may struggle to replicate for years to come.
 But that is precisely what makes the gamble so enormous. With a reported budget of Rs 2,000 crore, the film has little room for anything short of an exceptional performance. Its opening will be important, but sustaining audience interest, generating positive word of mouth and converting that interest into a long theatrical run will ultimately determine how far it goes.
 Ramayana: Rise of Legend , directed by Nitesh Tiwari, features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Yash as Raavan. The first part is slated to arrive in theatres on November 5, as the big Diwali release this year, with special previews scheduled for November 4 worldwide.
 The film is backed by Yash's Monster Mind Creations and Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios. - Ends Read more | Ramayana ticket prices surge upto Rs 3,170; fans raise affordability concerns
